title: Semiconductor Earnings Roundup: Revenue, Growth and Takeaways
gist: A company-by-company earnings roundup of 80 semiconductor companies shows AI-driven demand extending well beyond the usual suspects, with 11 companies posting triple-digit growth and all but 2 in positive territory. Memory/HBM, AI accelerators, advanced packaging, test and leading-edge manufacturing are the hottest growth areas, while handset and consumer results are mixed.

insights.claim: Across 80 semiconductor companies this quarter, 11 posted triple-digit year-over-year revenue growth and all but 2 were in positive territory, with AI infrastructure, memory, advanced packaging, test and leading-edge manufacturing the hottest growth areas.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Confirms an AI-driven upcycle broadening beyond mega-caps into the full supply chain—a signal that breadth, not just Nvidia, is carrying the sector.
insights.quote: Earnings were strong across all chip industry sectors this quarter, with 11 companies posting triple-digit growth, and all but 2 of the 80 companies reported here were in positive territory.

insights.claim: Micron Technology reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $41.46B, up 345.7% year over year, driven by record AI memory and HBM demand.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: A more-than-quadrupling of Micron revenue quantifies the severity of the memory upcycle.
insights.quote: AI memory and HBM demand drove record results.

insights.claim: SK hynix reported Q2 2026 revenue of $56.00B, up 257%, on record AI memory demand, and began mass shipments of HBM4.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: HBM4 mass shipments beginning marks the next-generation memory ramp that Nvidia/AMD accelerators depend on.
insights.quote: Record quarter on AI memory; HBM4 mass shipments began.

insights.claim: Kioxia Holdings revenue rose 415.5% and Sandisk rose 372%, both citing NAND pricing and AI/data-center demand, while Nanya Technology surged 684.2% on DRAM pricing with gross margin reaching 79.5%.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Extreme NAND and DRAM pricing gains show memory is the sharpest earnings leverage in the cycle.
insights.quote: DRAM pricing surged; gross margin reached 79.5%.

insights.claim: Samsung Electronics reported total Q2 2026 revenue of $121.08B, up 129.9%, with AI memory and HBM driving the semiconductor surge.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Confirms the memory upcycle is lifting the largest diversified players, not just pure-play memory makers.
insights.quote: AI memory and HBM drove the semiconductor surge.

insights.claim: NVIDIA reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.60B, up 85%, with Data Center revenue reaching $75.2B, up 92% year over year.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Nvidia data-center revenue near $75B sets the scale of AI capex flowing through the ecosystem.
insights.quote: Data Center reached $75.2B, up 92% year over year.

insights.claim: AMD reported Q2 2026 revenue of $11.54B, up 50.1%, with Data Center revenue reaching $6.7B, up 107% and now 58% of company revenue.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Data center becoming a majority of AMD revenue confirms it as a credible second AI-accelerator source.
insights.quote: Data Center revenue reached $6.7B, up 107% and 58% of company revenue.

insights.claim: Broadcom reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $22.19B, up 48%, with AI semiconductor revenue remaining the major growth engine.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Broadcom's custom-accelerator and networking franchise is a key beneficiary of hyperscaler AI buildout.
insights.quote: AI semiconductor revenue remained the major growth engine.

insights.claim: Cerebras Systems reported Q2 2026 GAAP revenue of $180.1M, up 74%, with cloud/services revenue rising 281%.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Cerebras' cloud surge shows non-GPU AI-compute challengers gaining commercial traction.
insights.quote: GAAP revenue; cloud/services revenue rose 281%.

insights.claim: TSMC reported Q2 2026 revenue of $40.20B, up 36%, with AI accelerators and leading-edge nodes remaining key growth drivers.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: TSMC is the shared manufacturing chokepoint monetizing nearly all leading-edge AI silicon.
insights.quote: AI accelerators and leading-edge nodes remained key growth drivers.

insights.claim: Intel reported Q2 2026 revenue of $16.10B, up 25%—its strongest growth in more than fifteen years—with DCAI growing strongly and Intel Foundry up 31%.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Intel's strongest growth in 15 years plus 31% foundry growth suggests a genuine turnaround inflection worth monitoring.
insights.quote: Strongest revenue growth in more than fifteen years; DCAI grew strongly. Intel Foundry up 31%.

insights.claim: Astera Labs reported Q2 2026 revenue of $392.4M, up 104% on exceptional AI-connectivity demand, guiding Q3 to $540M–$560M, while Credo more than doubled revenue with 157% growth on AI connectivity.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Connectivity-IP suppliers are among the fastest growers, reflecting interconnect as the AI-scaling bottleneck.
insights.quote: AI-connectivity demand remained exceptional; Q3 guided to $540M–$560M.

insights.claim: SiTime revenue rose 126.5% on AI infrastructure and LEO demand, and MaxLinear infrastructure revenue rose 145% led by optical AI-data-center adoption.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Timing and optical-infrastructure suppliers confirm demand for photonics and precision components in AI data centers.
insights.quote: Infrastructure revenue rose 145%, led by optical AI-data-center adoption.

insights.claim: Monolithic Power Systems reported Q2 2026 revenue of $980.6M, up 47.6%, with Enterprise Data revenue surging 164% driven by AI infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Power-management vendors ride the AI buildout as power delivery becomes a data-center constraint.
insights.quote: Enterprise Data revenue surged 164%, driven by AI infrastructure.

insights.claim: Test and assembly vendors surged: Teradyne rose 104% on AI-driven DRAM and NAND test, Kulicke & Soffa rose 122.6% on advanced-packaging and assembly demand, and Cohu's AI-compute test pipeline reached roughly $850M.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Back-end test and assembly is a strong secondary beneficiary as AI chip complexity raises testing intensity.
insights.quote: AI-driven DRAM and NAND test demand produced a record quarter.

insights.claim: Wafer-fab-equipment makers grew on AI-driven leading-edge and memory spend: Applied Materials $9.115B (+25%), Lam Research $6.72B (+30%), ASML $10.78B (+21.2%) on strong EUV demand, and KLA $3.66B (+15.2%).
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Broad WFE strength shows capex commitment to leading-edge and HBM capacity expansion.
insights.quote: Strong EUV and advanced-node demand supported a higher 2026 sales outlook.

insights.claim: Besi rose 68.7% on hybrid bonding, photonics and data-center packaging, while FormFactor set a record on HBM, foundry/logic and co-packaged-optics demand.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Hybrid bonding and co-packaged optics show up as concrete revenue drivers, validating those emerging packaging technologies.
insights.quote: Hybrid bonding, photonics and data-center packaging drove the sharp increase.

insights.claim: Synopsys revenue rose 41.9% as AI-driven chip complexity boosted EDA and IP demand and it raised its full-year outlook, while Cadence rose 24.2% and Arm's data-center royalties more than doubled.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: EDA/IP vendors compound on rising design complexity, a durable toll on the whole AI-silicon wave.
insights.quote: AI-driven chip complexity boosted demand across Synopsys’ EDA and IP portfolio; revenue beat guidance and the company raised its full-year outlook.

insights.claim: The only two of 80 companies not in positive territory were Qualcomm (-4%, handset revenue down 20% though Automotive and IoT grew) and Skyworks Solutions (-3.1%), highlighting handset/consumer softness against the AI boom.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: The bifurcation between AI-exposed and handset-exposed names is the key relative-value signal in the group.
insights.quote: Handset revenue fell 20%, while Automotive and IoT each grew strongly.

insights.claim: Silicon Labs suspended guidance amid a pending Texas Instruments acquisition, an M&A signal within the analog/embedded segment.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: A pending TI acquisition of Silicon Labs points to consolidation in analog/embedded even amid the AI-led upcycle.
insights.quote: guidance was suspended amid the pending TI acquisition.
